set.body:
Add a Scala.js-only surface-view-three adapter that interprets the shared SurfaceRenderPlan through a narrow facade over Three.js BufferGeometry, materials/shaders, cameras, render targets, and input events. Three.js types and mutable objects remain private to the adapter. Geometry, layer textures, colormap LUTs, thresholds, opacity, and camera dirty classes must respect the same resource keys and receipts as JavaFX. Render on demand except during gestures or playback.

Build a local differential harness against ~/code/jscode/surfviewjs using identical GIFTI geometry, fields, thresholds, cameras, and viewport sizes. Compare transformed bounds, landmark projections, per-vertex composited colors, selected face/vertex ids, semantic pixel regions, and performance counters; do not require exact antialiasing pixels.

Acceptance: shared JVM/JS core tests remain identical; browser tests cover context absence/loss, resize, disposal, and fallback errors; common SurfViewJS scalar/label/multilayer scenarios pass semantic differential checks; 32k/164k browser profiles capture draw calls, uploads, bytes, frame and pick latency; surfaceViewThreeJS/test and a live browser receipt pass.
set.title: Scala.js surface backend: thin Three.js adapter and SurfViewJS differential harness
